notes:
Account summary: Avalon is a freight orchestration and planning platform (global TMS) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production ML inference. They want reserved GPU pools across NA/EU with automatic cross-region failover. Primary driver: avoid model cold-start latency and unpredictable preemptible capacity when routing customer-facing chat and reranking.

Key requirements (raw from calls):
- Workloads: high-volume chat (session-based), per-request reranking for route-optimization, embeddings for similarity search.
- Traffic profile: 1.8k concurrent sessions peak, average 450 qps to generation endpoints, peaks at 1.2k qps during morning batch windows; embeddings jobs batched overnight ~20k reqs/hr.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms for chat response tokens (incl. network to Redwood edge), p95 < 200ms for reranking endpoints.
- Throughput guarantees: sustained throughput of 10k tokens/sec cluster-wide with burst up to 30k tokens/sec for 60s windows. Want explicit per-region throughput baselines and documented throttling behavior.
- Failover/headroom: require minimum 25% reserve headroom per region for AZ failure, desire cross-region warm standby able to take full load within T+60s with degraded latency budget.
- Model strategy: primary gpt-ensemble quantized variants for cost, fallback to smaller low-latency model on overload. Must support pinned model versions per route.
- Data & compliance: EU residency for EU accounts, audit logs for all inference requests, KMS-managed keys for embeddings.
- Ops: need token-level cost breakdowns, trace IDs in console, and routing policy controls to prefer low-latency region under 120ms RTT.

Conversations / quotes:
- "We cannot accept more than 10% of requests seeing >300ms p95 during peak — customers churn quickly." — Head of Product (11/30 call).
- "If Redwood can guarantee throughput for 2x our 2025 forecast load with cross-region failover, procurement will recommend Reserved plan." — VP Engineering (12/04).

Procurement & technical path:
- 2024-11-20: kickoff sizing call (Fireflies ff_2024-11-20_avalon_sizing). initial metrics sent (qps, token sizes, session lengths).
- 2024-11-27: Redwood SE (Mateo) delivered preliminary reserved GPU counts per region (NA: 40 GPUs, EU: 20 GPUs) with 25% AZ headroom recommendation. shared in drive:/decks/avalon_sizing_deck_v2.pdf.
- 2024-11-30: SLA negotiation: discussed measurable SLOs, crediting policy for cross-region failover (Fireflies ff_2024-11-30_sla_negotiation). Legal requested formula for credits if failover causes sustained latency degradation >30% for >10 minutes.
- 2024-12-03: Security deep-dive; checklist items: encryption-in-transit, KMS integration, SOC2 attestation check, on-prem DR runbook request (SEC-2047).
- 2024-12-04: Sizing workshop scheduled to validate perf numbers with Redwood POC (3-day POC simulating peak traffic).

POC plan (agreed):
- Day 0: deploy dedicated pool in NA with pinned model variant; run synthetic traffic shaped to 450 qps steady + 1.2k qps spike windows.
- Day 1: induce AZ failure in NA to validate 25% headroom assumption and measure cross-region cold-start time to EU warm standby.
- Day 2: run long-tail latency tests, quantify throttling thresholds, and validate billing/cost telemetry. deliverables: latency heatmaps, token throughput charts, failover RTO/RPO metrics.

Open technical questions (action items):
- How does Redwood compute regional throughput when KV cache prefixing is used across sessions? (Action: Mateo to confirm implementation detail 2024-12-06).
- Exact SLA credit formula for multi-region failover where Redwood routes to alternate region (Legal/Finance want worst-case credit capped).
- Need a runbook snippet for on-prem DR tie-in; Avalon wants ability to run critical reranking on customer-owned capacity if cloud regions fail.

Sales/Finance notes:
- Pricing sensitivity: Avalon prefers a blended committed rate with defined burst allowance at a higher overage price. expect negotiations on 36-month contract.
- Procurement expects to trade a higher committed ARR for a lower per-token rate and guaranteed throughput lanes.

Recommended Redwood internal next steps (AE/SE):
- Provide a formal capacity plan per region/AZ with explicit headroom % and fallback flow diagrams by 2024-12-09.
- Prepare a POC checklist and synthetic workload scripts (shared repo) before workshop.
- Draft SLA amendment language that covers cross-region failover credits and measurement windows (legal ticket INFR-4821).
